prompt: Implement src/limiter.js exporting `createLimiter({ capacity, refillPerSec, now = Date.now })`, a per-key token-bucket rate limiter. It returns `{ take(key, cost = 1), peek(key) }`. Each key starts with a full bucket of `capacity` tokens and refills continuously at `refillPerSec` tokens per second (fractional refill allowed, never above capacity). `take` returns `{ ok: true, remaining }` and consumes `cost` tokens when enough are available, otherwise `{ ok: false, remaining, retryAfterMs }` without consuming anything, where retryAfterMs is the whole number of milliseconds (rounded up) until enough tokens will be available. `cost` greater than capacity always fails with `retryAfterMs: Infinity`. `remaining` is the number of tokens left, rounded down to an integer. `peek(key)` returns the current token count (rounded down) without consuming. Time comes only from `now()` (milliseconds). Write your own tests in test/ and run `node --test` (it finds test/*.test.mjs; on Node 24 `node --test test/` fails because a directory argument is not accepted).
